title: Landfall and Summit
premise: Noor Ashgrove, a riverboat captain who has spent years outrunning her family's name and the debts attached to it, is hired to trace the disappearance of a government survey team that vanished near the river's forbidden headwaters. Following their abandoned gear and a trail of impossible clues, she discovers the team found something at the source worth killing for—and that one survivor, a young cartographer named Idris, is being hunted by the very agency that sent them. Forced to choose between delivering Idris to safety and claiming an inheritance she never wanted, Noor finally stops running: she claims her grandmother's landfall claim at the river's mouth, using its legal weight to shield her found family and expose the survey's cover-up.
about_author: Bram Oyelaran is a former deckhand turned novelist who spent a decade working inland waterways before trading the wheelhouse for a writing desk. Their fiction draws on river lore, salvage stories, and the people who live where maps go soft.

chapters.title: The Weight of Water
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Hired by a nervous government liaison to investigate the vanished survey team, Noor plans to take the money and report nothing—until she finds the team's boat moored and empty, gear intact, no tracks on either bank. The emotional beat is reluctance: every instinct tells her to walk away, but the sight of a child's carved toy among the equipment hooks something she thought she'd buried.

chapters.title: What the Current Keeps
chapters.summary: Alternating Noor's POV with journal entries from the missing team. Upstream, Noor finds Idris, the team's junior cartographer, hiding in a flooded quarry—he saw what his superiors did to protect the source's secret. Pursuers close in. The emotional beat is wary trust: two people who survive by not belonging to anyone begin, grudgingly, to belong to each other.

chapters.title: Headwaters
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, climax. Racing the thaw-swollen river to the source, Noor and Idris are cornered by the survey chief, who reveals the inheritance angle: the 'forbidden' land sits inside the Ashgrove family's lapsed landfall claim, and only a living Ashgrove can seal or sell it. In a storm at the spring itself, Noor refuses the bribe, saves Idris from drowning, and lets the evidence wash downstream to allies below.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, resolution. Back at the river mouth, Noor files the claim she spent her life avoiding—not as an escape from duty but as a use of it—anchoring the legal fight that clears Idris's name and exposes the survey's crimes. The emotional beat is arrival: the woman who kept moving plants her feet, opens her dockside house to strays, and learns that stopping costs less than she feared when you're not stopping alone.
